implementation_strategy: Execute preregistered paired confirmatory bank (200 tasks) using the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter: for each task run the shared initial generation (baseline) and the guarded GVR transformation per adapter contract; all validators, scorers, and deployment checks are deterministic and executed in Docker; stop when all tasks executed or when maximum_model_calls (400) reached.
public_resources: Deterministic verifier and translator code (public repo)
model_and_version_plan: gpt-5-mini (use hosted API endpoint; version gpt-5-mini)
task_manifest_strategy: Deterministic mapping file (intent→template id) with fixed RNG seed; manifest lists exactly 200 confirmatory task ids (1..200) and 50 exploratory ids; all entries hashed and published.
transformation_manifest_strategy: Use adapter-declared transformations: direct_configuration_generation_v1 for baseline and generate_validate_repair_v1 for guarded; all translator/verifier unit tests executed in CI (Docker) and outputs hashed.
randomisation_plan: Task order randomized with fixed seed per preregistration; within each batch tasks executed in randomized order using same seed mapping stored in manifest.
caching_plan: Cache no model outputs beyond adapter-provided transient logs; deterministic verifier artifacts cached in Docker volumes for reproducibility only; no reuse to exceed model-call budget.
failure_recovery_plan: Infrastructure failures (container crashes) logged and triggers automated re-execution up to preregistered retry policy (recover infrastructure only); verifier/logging failures trigger re-execution once; re-executions counted toward maximum_model_calls.
result_schema: paired_binary_episode_v1 (per-task: task_id, condition, model_output, deterministic_verifier_result (accept/reject), deployment_trace, operational_failure_indicator, provenance_hashes)
estimated_compute_notes: All model calls via hosted openai_responses gpt-5-mini API. Maximum planned model calls = 400 (200 tasks × up to 2 calls). Verifier and translator run on CPU in Docker; no local GPU required.
